artist.name: Leonora Carrington
artist.bio: Mary Leonora Carrington was a British and Mexican surrealist painter and novelist. She lived most of her adult life in Mexico City and was one of the last surviving participants in the Surrealist movement of the 1930s. Carrington was also a founding member of the women's liberation movement in Mexico during the 1970s.

summary:
Australia is navigating a pivotal moment in its demographic and economic future, highlighted by the release of the seventh Intergenerational Report. Projections indicate the population will approach 40 million by 2066, driven by increased life expectancy and migration, prompting national conversations about productivity, social support, and sustainability. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is leveraging this context to launch Australia’s bid for a United Nations Security Council seat, emphasizing the nation’s reputation for stability and international cooperation while advocating for human-centric AI governance.

On the ground, community resilience and care are taking center stage. In Victoria, advocates are pushing for expanded mental health services in the Wimmera region, highlighting the need for local access to support those with high rates of illness. Simultaneously, a landmark survey reveals gaps in dementia care, prompting calls for better integration of support systems for overwhelmed carers. These stories underscore a collective effort to strengthen social safety nets and ensure no one is left behind during life’s challenging transitions.

Internationally, scientific curiosity and human achievement continue to drive progress. Researchers have made significant strides in understanding Alzheimer’s disease by mapping 3D DNA organization, while astronomers have identified the largest newly formed impact crater in the Solar System. In sports, Australia’s Rollers celebrated a historic victory in the IWBF World Championships, showcasing excellence and unity. These global developments reflect a world increasingly focused on health, exploration, and the power of human ingenuity.
